info.title: x402 Receive Service
info.description: Synthex Forge x402 Receive: 41 paid verification, attestation and governance endpoints (Ed25519 + SHA-256 signed artifacts) plus free verify/public-key/standard sibling routes. Paid routes answer HTTP 402 with an x402 v2 `payment-required` envelope (atomic USDC on Base mainnet, chain ID 8453). Free routes are declared with `security: []` per the x402scan discovery spec.
info.x-guidance: Agents: every paid route answers 402 with a base64 `Payment-Required` header containing `accepts[]` with `asset=USDC` on `network=base` and `payTo` set to the Synthex Forge receive address. Sign with the EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization flow, then resubmit the request with an `X-PAYMENT` header carrying the signed payload. Each paid route is paired with a free /verify or /public-key sibling — call those to independently verify any paid artifact without paying again. The public-key routes return the Ed25519 hex keys; the verify routes take the signed artifact_id and return a verification verdict. Governance routes (/v1/governance/*) implement an atomic reserved-lease spend-gate: reserve → act → settle against the same lease_id. The Verification Bureau routes (/v1/bureau/*) score other x402 services against a public standard and feed a public corpus.

get.summary: Prepaid pass balance — read-only, does not consume a call
get.description:
FREE: how many calls are left on a prepaid capacity pass.

READ-ONLY. This route NEVER consumes a call, never decrements a
balance and never writes to the ledger — it is the check you can run
as often as you like.

A wrong, malformed, expired, exhausted or unknown token returns HTTP
200 with `valid: false` and a machine-readable `reason`. It does NOT
return 402 (this route is free) and it does NOT return 500 (a bad
token is a routine outcome, not a fault).

get.description: Free route. GET /ping. No payment required. Error codes and their remedies are published at https://x402.synthexforge.com/v1/errors.

FREE: the measured status of this service, signed.

RESPONSE {status, uptime_pct_24h, uptime_pct_7d, uptime_pct_30d,
coverage_hours_24h, coverage_hours_7d, coverage_pct_7d, probes_24h,
failed_probes_24h, checks[{target, ok, latency_ms, last_probe}],
incidents[{target, start, end, summary}], build{version, deployed_at},
windows, methodology, generated_at, signature, sha256, key_id, signedBy,
publicKeyHex}.

status is 'operational' | 'degraded' | 'outage' | 'unknown'. It is
DERIVED from the 24h window: below 95% uptime is 'degraded', below 50%
is 'outage', and a window we barely covered is 'degraded' because we
cannot prove the service was up when we were not looking. With no probe
rows at all the status is 'unknown' — never a fabricated 'operational'.

The signature is Ed25519 over the canonical JSON (sort_keys=true,
separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=false) of the body WITHOUT the
signature/sha256/key_id/signedBy/publicKeyHex fields, so a buyer can
strip those five and recompute both the hash and the signature from the
body alone. The preimage spec and the public key are at
GET /v1/status/public-key.

get.summary: The status attestation signing key and preimage spec
get.description:
FREE: the Ed25519 public key + the signature preimage spec.

The preimage a buyer must reconstruct to verify a /v1/status body:

    canonical = json.dumps(body_without_signature_fields,
                           sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'),
                           ensure_ascii=True).encode('utf-8')
    signature = Ed25519_sign(canonical), hex
    sha256    = SHA-256(canonical), hex

`body_without_signature_fields` means: drop 'signature', 'sha256',
'key_id', 'signedBy' and 'publicKeyHex' from the returned body.

NOTE on ensure_ascii: this service's canonical serialisation is
json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) with the DEFAULT
ensure_ascii=True. That is what the signing key actually signed, so that
is what a verifier must reproduce. (The published spec was briefly wrong
on 2026-10-21 and was corrected after an independent verification
attempt failed — the signature was always valid, the description was not.)

post.summary: Verify a /v1/status body (free)
post.description:
FREE: independently verify a /v1/status body you received.

POST the body you got from GET /v1/status and this recomputes the
SHA-256 and checks the Ed25519 signature against our public key, using
the SAME canonical rule the signer used. If the body was altered after
we signed it, this says so.

RESPONSE {valid, signature_valid, hash_valid, recomputed_sha256,
verified_by, verified_at}.

402.description: Payment Required — x402 challenge in the Payment-Required response header and/or JSON body. See x-payment-info on this operation for price/network. When an `X-Zeux-Pass` header is supplied, the 402 body carries a machine-readable `error_reason` instead of the generic `payment_required`: `pass_expired` (the pass has expired), `pass_exhausted` (no calls remaining), `pass_scope` (the pass does not cover a route at this price), `pass_invalid_signature` (the token signature did not verify), `pass_malformed` (the token is not a well-formed token), `pass_unknown` (the pass is not known to this service). A pass is never a free pass-through: every one of these refusals leaves the caller to pay per call. Error codes and their remedies are published at https://x402.synthexforge.com/v1/errors.

parameters.description: Optional idempotency key. When a pass is used, the same key on the same pass NEVER double-decrements the balance — a retried request is replayed, not recharged.

parameters.name: X-Zeux-Pass
parameters.description: OPTIONAL prepaid-capacity pass token. When present and valid, the call is authorised against the pass balance instead of being billed per call. The token is self-verifying: Ed25519 over `pass_id|route_scope|calls_total|expires_at`, so it can be checked without a database read. Scope `micro_le_0.25` authorises only routes priced at or below $0.25 — a pass on a more expensive route is refused with 402 `pass_scope`. A pass never bypasses payment: an invalid, expired, exhausted, out-of-scope or tampered pass is refused with a machine-readable 402 reason and the buyer must pay per call. OMITTING this header leaves the request behaviour byte-identical to paying per call.

post.summary: Output Verify
post.description:
Agent Output Verification Engine — grade ONE caller-supplied agent
output on FIVE deterministic legs and return ONE signed, reproducible verdict.

Price $0.50 / 500000 atomic. Verdict in {PASS, PASS-WITH-CAVEATS, FAIL,
INSUFFICIENT-DATA}. Deterministic pure-function engine (output_kb.py):
no lookahead, no leaks, no fabricated data, no LLM, no network fetch. If
fewer than 2 of 5 legs are assessable, the verdict is honestly withheld
as INSUFFICIENT-DATA (never invented).

Reconstruct what happened across a payment and its workflow.

Price $0.25 / 250000 atomic per investigation. Deterministic
pure-function engine (`control_plane/forensics_kb.py`): no clock, no
network, no randomness in the decision path.

Honest-answer boundary: an EMPTY evidence set returns UNRESOLVED, never
a finding. The absence of evidence is not evidence of wrongdoing. The
report has no accusation vocabulary, and the four classes are structural:
a provider-supplied statement CANNOT reach `verified_facts`.

Integrity boundary: `receipt_valid`, `chain_valid` and
`delivery_confirmed` are reported SEPARATELY. A valid signature proves
the record was signed by that key — it does not prove a provider
delivered what it promised.

Fabrication boundary: a transaction detail that cannot be read is `null`
with the reason named in `unresolved`. Nothing is invented.

Read-only boundary: no outbound call, no store write, no settlement. This
service investigates; it cannot move money and cannot change a record.

Return ONE signed, replayable OHLCV snapshot for an instrument.

source hash, so a decision can be replayed against exactly the candles
it was taken on.

unparseable timestamp or a reversed window returns HTTP 400 with verdict
"CANNOT_DETERMINE" — the service NEVER defaults to a successful snapshot
on bad input. An instrument absent from the store, or a window with no
rows, returns verdict "CANNOT_DETERMINE" with a named reason; it is
NEVER presented as an empty-but-successful snapshot.

Bounded-scan boundary: `limit` is clamped to [1, 20000] and every read
is an indexed range scan. An unbounded request can never reach the
123M-row table.

Historical-data boundary: this is HISTORICAL DATA, not a live price
oracle. The `asOf` field reports the timestamp of the NEWEST BAR IN THE
SNAPSHOT, not the wall clock. It carries NO settlement meaning and must
not be used to mark a position to market.

post.summary: Signed bar series over an explicit range (PAID $1.00)
post.description:
Return ONE bar series over an explicit [start, end] range, with a
signed manifest.

Price $1.00 / 1000000 atomic per series.

THE RANGE ROUTE. `POST /v1/market/snapshot` is the TAIL route (the
latest N bars of one instrument) and stays at $0.01. The two never
return the same thing: a snapshot request whose window starts more than
30 days back is rejected with HTTP 400 and a pointer at this route.

CAPS: 1 instrument, <= 50,000 bars, range <= 2 years. Exceeding a cap
returns HTTP 400 carrying the ACTUAL counts (`requested_bars`,
`limit`) — never a silent truncation.

THE MANIFEST carries exactly {source, licence, instrument, timeframe,
start, end, rows, first_ts, last_ts, gaps, sha256, generated_at,
key_id, signature}. `sha256` is SHA-256 over the canonical
serialisation of the series payload — recomputable by the buyer from
the returned body alone. `signature` is Ed25519 over the preimage
`sha256_RAW_BYTES || generated_at_utf8 || rows_decimal_utf8`.

THE GAP REPORT is truthful: the expected bar count for the window is
compared against the observed rows and contiguous missing spans are
listed as {from, to, bars_missing}. An empty `gaps` list means
VERIFIED COMPLETE, never "not checked".

COVERAGE: Binance holds M1 for the trailing 90 days and H1/D1 from
2018-01-01 (or the instrument's listing date, whichever is later) to
now; the ECB holds daily reference rates from 1999. The manifest
reports the MEASURED first_ts / last_ts / rows — never an assumed
range. M5 / M15 / H4 are resampled from the M1 base, so they agree
with it exactly.

LICENCE: the data is the Binance official public bulk archive or the
European Central Bank euro foreign-exchange reference rates, and every
response and manifest carries that attribution. Restricted vendor
FXTrade Rates are never served.

Re-verify for free at POST /v1/market/history/verify; the Ed25519
public key and the signature preimage spec are at
GET /v1/market/history/public-key.

FREE: the Ed25519 public key + the signature preimage spec.

The preimage a buyer must reconstruct to verify a manifest:

    sha256_RAW_BYTES  = the 32 raw bytes of the manifest's `sha256` hex

of the `series` payload: stable JSON with sort_keys=true,
separators=(',',':') and ensure_ascii=false. For format='csv' the
payload is the CSV string, so the hash is over those exact bytes.

offer against standard v1.0.0 — not just our own artifacts.

get.summary: x402 Bureau — the dated, append-only observation corpus (FREE)
get.description:
FREE: the public, append-only record of what the Bureau actually observed.

APPEND-ONLY contract: records are never rewritten or deleted. A correction is
an ADDITIONAL record linked by `supersedes`; the original stays on disk
forever. Records are re-read from disk on every request (the service runs
multi-worker; the filesystem is the only cross-process serializer), so this
view is always consistent. Every record carries `coverage_gaps` naming what
was NOT observed — a corpus that implies completeness it lacks is worse than
none. Presented newest-first.

against a promise we never saw.

Extract the money-and-liability clauses from a commercial agreement,
by RULE, and sign the result.

model in the answer path. A clause is located in two steps: the section
whose heading matches the clause group, then the group's published

disagreement (two different expiry dates, two different caps) is

not pick one.

post.description:
The order gate — call it BEFORE every order.

Price $0.25 / 250000 atomic per gate call. The caller submits
{account{equity,currency}, positions[], order{symbol,side,notional,price,
sl}, limits{...}, as_of}.

The verdict is one of:
  approve   every check passes at the requested size.
  reduce    a limit is breached, but a SMALLER size passes. The response
            carries `approved_notional` — a size that ACTUALLY passes
            every check, and `approved_checks` showing the check set
            evaluated AT that size.
  reject    no size passes (e.g. the account is already at its
            open-position limit), so the order must be re-specified.
  insufficient_input  the request does not carry what the checks need;
            `missing_fields` NAMES the absent field. No verdict is
            guessed and no limit is assumed.

Six named checks run, each reported with its limit, the observed value
and the result: per_trade_risk, gross_exposure, open_positions,
instrument_weight, correlated_exposure (against a static, versioned,
documented bucket table shipped with the answer) and margin_headroom.

The binding constraint is the rule with the TIGHTEST actual ceiling, so
it names the limit that really decides the answer.

Certify one portfolio against one mandate, and sign the certificate.

Price $5.00 / 5000000 atomic per certificate. The caller submits
{mandate{max_drawdown, max_single_asset_weight, allowed_asset_classes,
max_leverage, min_liquidity_score}, portfolio{nav, positions[],

The verdict is one of:
  compliant      every mandated rule is satisfied by the supplied data.
  breach         at least one rule is violated; every breach carries
                 its limit, the actual value, a severity (graded on the
                 OVERSHOOT past the limit) and a remediation.
  indeterminate  the data does not decide the question. The reasons are
                 named in `indeterminate_reasons`.

`indeterminate` is returned when an asset class in the portfolio is NOT
listed in the mandate's `allowed_asset_classes` (the engine does not
decide whether an unlisted class is prohibited or merely unmentioned),
or when a MANDATED metric was not supplied. The engine NEVER certifies
`compliant` when a mandated metric is missing — that is the rule this
service exists to hold.

Every check is reported, including the ones that passed, so the reader
sees the whole evidence base. The certificate carries its
`methodology_version`, so a reader can tell which rule set produced it.

post.summary: How much money can this strategy actually carry? Capacity with the binding constraint and the degradation curve (PAID $10.00)
post.description:
Size the book: how much capital can this strategy carry before the
edge is gone?

Price $10.00 / 10000000 atomic per capacity answer. The caller submits
{strategy{type,instrument,timeframe,trades_per_month,avg_hold_hours,
sharpe,win_rate,avg_rr}, capital{aum_usd,max_cost_bps_of_alpha},
market{adv_usd,spread_bps,impact_coefficient}, as_of}.

The verdict is one of:
  capacity_computed  the model ran and produced a number.
  insufficient_input the request does not carry what the model needs;
                    `missing_fields` NAMES the absent field. A missing
                    `adv_usd` is never replaced with a guess.
  no_capacity        the answer is genuinely ZERO — the spread alone
                    already exceeds the whole cost budget, so no size
                    of this strategy is worth running. A real answer,
                    not a failure.

The answer carries the capacity, a band around it, the BINDING
constraint (market impact, steady-state participation, or the unwind),
the alpha after costs, and a degradation curve showing the edge
decaying as the book grows.

The impact model is stated in the response with its provenance — a
square-root (Almgren-style) law — and every parameter is overridable
and every default is named in `assumptions`. Capacity DECREASES as the
assumed Sharpe falls, and the self-test asserts it.

The calibration block is an anonymised aggregate from our own graded
strategy vault: the prior that an edge of this shape and instrument is
real, and the depth of the evidence behind it. It is REPORTED beside
the headline; the headline capacity is computed at the caller's own
asserted Sharpe with no prior haircut, and a prior-adjusted capacity
is returned separately.

The only on-chain movement is the price of the answer.

post.description:
Prove the execution was in line with the mandate — the artefact that
makes an agent's execution auditable rather than merely fast.

Price $2.00 / 2000000 atomic per attestation. The caller submits
{order{symbol,side,notional,decision_price,arrival_time,
target_strategy,tolerance_bps}, fills[{time,price,quantity}],
benchmarks{arrival,vwap,interval_vwap,primary,adv_usd,
interval_duration_hours}, as_of}.

The verdict is one of:
  within_tolerance       the execution was inside the stated tolerance
                         against the benchmark the answer names.
  outside_tolerance      it was outside.
  insufficient_evidence  the evidence does not support a verdict, and
                         the response NAMES what is missing. There are
                         exactly three ways to earn it: no arrival
                         price (implementation shortfall is undefined
                         without one), fills that do not sum to the
                         notional within 1bp, or a malformed price or
                         quantity.

The response carries the implementation shortfall, the slippage
against the arrival price, the gap to every benchmark supplied, the
timing risk, the participation rate where it can be computed, and a
quality grade. Every bps figure is reproducible from the numbers
shown: the arithmetic is written into `findings`.

The benchmark the verdict is taken against is NAMED in the response.
"Within tolerance" against the arrival price and against the interval
VWAP are different claims, and the engine never picks one silently.

PAID $0.05: has this been tested before, and what was the result?

The registry reads our own strategy vault READ-ONLY — 433 prior tests
with their grades, sample sizes and the REASON each one failed. It
never writes to the vault and never regrades an entry.

and coverage_gaps=["no_prior_test"]. The service NEVER answers "edge
confirmed" and NEVER invents a grade — a caller must be able to trust
the negative answer as much as the positive one.

CONTAMINATED RESULTS ARE REPORTED, NEVER COUNTED. An entry whose
status marks it as lookahead-biased is still shown to the caller
(hiding it would be its own dishonesty) but it is excluded from
clean_evidence. If the ONLY matches are contaminated, clean_evidence is
false and the summary says so in words.

MATCH RANKING (published and deterministic): the tuple
(tier, instrument_rank, timeframe_rank, strategy_rank, family_rank,
-text_overlap, name, id), where tier 0 is an exact
instrument+timeframe hit, 1 an exact instrument hit on another
timeframe, 2 a family or strategy_type hit, and 3 a free-text token
overlap. Exact instrument+timeframe ALWAYS ranks above a family match.

OUTPUT WHITELIST: only aggregate fields are exposed — no filesystem
paths, no internal notes, no account references, no keys, no PII.

DETERMINISM: no LLM anywhere, no clock in the signed core, so the same
query always produces the same output_sha256.

post.description:
PAID $3.00: is that track record real, or did you find it by looking?

Returns ONE of four verdicts — `replicable`, `likely_overfit`,
`not_replicable` or `insufficient_evidence` — with the full
arithmetic behind it, the published thresholds that produced it, and
an anonymised base rate from our own graded vault.

THE ARITHMETIC IS OURS AND REPRODUCIBLE. The Deflated Sharpe is the
house implementation, LIFTED VERBATIM from
/root/.hermes/pipeline/workspace/_audit_dsr_oct03.py into
engine/edge_dsr.py — one formula in the house, not two. The PBO and
the OOS calibration are published in the OpenAPI description and
echoed in `assumptions`.

TRIALS_ATTEMPTED IS MANDATORY. A missing trial count is a 400 that
names the field, and a single trial is refused outright: the
expected-maximum-Sharpe approximation is undefined at N=1 and would
report maximum confidence for a one-configuration search.

`insufficient_evidence` IS A FIRST-CLASS ANSWER, not a failure. It is
returned whenever the input cannot support a verdict — too few
observations, a zero-variance series, or a missing trial count — and
it names exactly what is needed.

THE CALIBRATION IS AN ANONYMISED AGGREGATE from our own graded
vault, published only at n >= 5. No strategy name, no file path, no
grade reason ever appears.

  n < 100 (daily)                 => insufficient_evidence
  n < 30  (per_trade)             => insufficient_evidence
  zero variance                   => insufficient_evidence
  trials_attempted missing        => insufficient_evidence
  trials_attempted < 2            => 400 (the expected-maximum-Sharpe
                                    approximation is undefined for a
                                    single trial)

post.description:
BioTrust Service 14 — Registry Verification.

Price $0.75 / 750000 atomic per verification check.

WHAT THIS IS: a registry-verification engine. It answers one question
— "is this person, institution, paper or company real, and is this
name on a sanctions list, with a citation and a timestamp for every
answer?" — by querying the public ORCID, ROR, OpenAlex (with a
Crossref fallback) and UK Companies House registries, and by
screening a name against the official OFAC, EU and UK OFSI
consolidated sanctions lists that were ingested at BUILD TIME.

WHAT `found` MEANS: exactly "a record of this identifier exists in
this registry at this time". It is NOT "the person is trustworthy",
NOT "the supplier is safe", NOT "the paper is sound", and it is NOT
an endorsement of anything.

THE SANCTIONS VERDICT VOCABULARY: `no_match`, `possible_match`,
`ambiguous`, `provider_unavailable`, `stale_index`. There is NO
`sanctioned` verdict and NO `safe` verdict — the service never
decides that anyone is sanctioned, and it never clears them either.
It surfaces CANDIDATES for a human, with the list, the entry id and
the matched name for each. A `possible_match` sets
`human_review_required: true`; it is NOT a determination.

THE SCOPE BOUNDARY: this service does NOT verify personal
identity documents (KYC) and does NOT verify professional
credentials. No passport, driving licence, national identity
number, degree, licence or professional registration is checked
here. A valid ORCID, ROR id, DOI or company number proves that an
IDENTIFIER EXISTS — it does NOT prove that a person is
trustworthy, that a supplier is safe to do business with, or that a
publication is sound.

A PROVIDER FAILURE is a `degraded` envelope carrying a
`provider_unavailable` verdict and a reason. A lookup that failed
NEVER produces a found result, and a result is NEVER invented.

DETERMINISTIC: no LLM. The sanctions matching is pure Python over a
committed index; the registry lookups are bounded, cached fetches.

post.description:
BioTrust Service 01 — BioRisk.

Price $2.00 / 2000000 atomic per declared-setup review record.

WHAT THIS IS: a STRUCTURED REVIEW RECORD over a DECLARED
institutional setup. The caller declares — in a closed, enum-only
vocabulary — the kind of work, the agent risk group, the containment
level, the activity modifiers, and the controls already in place.
The service matches that declaration against a documented control
matrix whose every rule cites a document in the published compliance
corpus, and returns:

  * the controls the published guidance associates with the
    declaration, and which of them are NOT declared;
  * the review steps a qualified human must carry out, each tied to
    the rule that requires it;
  * what could not be determined, and why.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: a biological assessment. It does NOT score a
pathogen, does NOT rank an agent's danger, does NOT infer hazard from
anything the caller did not explicitly declare, and does NOT produce
a number that could be read as "this work is safe". The `risk_tier`
is a CORRESPONDENCE between the declared containment level and the
published containment band for it, returned with its `basis` so the
caller can see exactly what produced it, and it is explicitly
advisory.

THE SCHEMA IS ENUM-ONLY, AND THAT IS A SAFETY CONTROL. There is no
free-text field anywhere in the request. A pathogen name, a sequence,
a method, a quantity and a protocol have nowhere to enter — a
request that tries to supply one is REFUSED with `unknown_field`
before it reaches the engine. Do not add a `description` or a
`notes` field to this model: that would open the injection surface

post.summary: Is this edge deployable? Deflated Sharpe with a calibrated multiple-testing threshold (PAID $2.00)
post.description:
Return ONE signed, dated strategy verdict.

Price $2.00 / 2000000 atomic per verdict. The caller submits a return
series; the engine returns deployable | candidate | reject |
insufficient_data with the reasoning attached.

THE DEFLATED SHARPE. The observed Sharpe is adjusted for the number of
independent attempts the caller (or our own vault) implies, using the
Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014) construction. The threshold is the
Sharpe the BEST of N lucky attempts would be expected to reach — which
is why a backtest that was selected from hundreds cannot clear it by
accident.

THE TWO HARD RULES:
  * fewer than 250 observations returns `insufficient_data` with the
    count named — NEVER a verdict. A confident answer on thin data is
    worse than an honest refusal.
  * a verdict is NEVER `deployable` when the deflated Sharpe is below
    the multiple-testing threshold. That assertion is a mutation test,
    not a comment.

THE STABILITY BLOCK. The series is cut into four contiguous subperiods
and each one's information ratio is reported, together with the WORST
of them — because the worst subperiod is the number that describes the
drawdown an allocator would have lived through.

Read-only boundary: this service NEVER settles, debits, or moves funds.
The only on-chain movement is the price of the answer.

post.description:
Return ONE signed, dated significance test.

Price $0.05 / 50000 atomic per test. The caller submits a return
series; the engine returns significant | not_significant |
insufficient_data with the p-value and the correction attached.

THE TEST IS NOT VACUOUS. A permutation test on a permutation-INVARIANT
quantity measures nothing: reordering cannot change the statistic, so
every permutation gives the same value and the p-value is meaningless.
This test uses a SIGN-FLIP null on the information ratio — the sign
flip preserves the marginal distribution and the autocorrelation while
destroying the mean structure, and the resulting null distribution is
genuinely dispersed.

THE TEST IS ONE-SIDED AND POSITIVE. The question is "is there a
PROFITABLE edge?". A strongly negative mean is not an edge, and this
service will not report it as significant.

THE NULL IS SEEDED. The same request yields the same p-value in any
process, so the `output_sha256` is an identifier rather than a
timestamp.

post.summary: Can this sizing scheme bankrupt me? First-passage ruin probability with Kelly (PAID $0.05)
post.description:
Return ONE signed, dated risk-of-ruin answer.

Price $0.05 / 50000 atomic per answer. The caller submits the trade
statistics and the sizing scheme; the engine returns safe | cautious |
excessive | ruin_dominant | insufficient_input with the Kelly and
half-Kelly fractions beside it.

THE MODEL IS STATED, NOT IMPLIED. The stake is FIXED at
`risk_per_trade_pct` of the initial capital on every trade, so the
equity is an additive random walk and the ruin probability is the
classical first-passage formula (Dubins & Savage). The full form is
published in the `assumptions` block.

RUIN IS ABSORBING: once equity reaches zero it stays zero, in the
simulation as well as in the model.

THE TWO NUMBERS. The analytic probability AND a seeded simulation of
the same process are both reported. If they disagree by more than
0.05, the response says so explicitly rather than presenting one of
them as the truth.

THE INPUT GATE: a win rate outside (0, 1), a non-positive
`avg_loss_r`, a non-positive risk fraction, a non-positive capital or
a non-positive trade count each return `insufficient_input` — no
value is guessed.

post.description:
Return ONE signed, dated overlap matrix.

Price $0.10 / 100000 atomic per matrix. The caller submits the
strategies and their return series; the engine returns the pairwise
correlations, the crowded pairs, the clusters, and the verdict
independent | partially_correlated | crowded | insufficient_data.

THE INSUFFICIENT-PAIR RULE. A pair with fewer than 60 overlapping
observations is OMITTED and COUNTED in `insufficient_pairs`. It is
never zero-filled: a zero correlation is a MEASUREMENT ("these move
together not at all"), and confusing it with "we could not measure it"
is the exact error this route exists to prevent. The omitted pairs are
named in `coverage_gaps`.

THE CLUSTERS. Connected components of the crowded-pair graph — two
strategies that are both crowded with a third belong to the same
cluster even if they are not directly comparable to each other.

PRIVACY: the `id` is the caller's own label and is echoed back. Nothing
about our vault is exposed.

post.summary: What does the equity curve look like? Seeded distribution of terminal outcomes (PAID $0.15)
post.description:
Return ONE signed, dated Monte Carlo distribution.

Price $0.15 / 150000 atomic per distribution. The caller submits the
trade distribution, the horizon and a SEED; the engine returns the
terminal-outcome percentiles, the probability of profit, and the p50
and p95 maximum drawdown.

THE SEED IS THE DETERMINISM. The same seed yields the same
distribution — and therefore the same `output_sha256` — in any
process, on any machine, forever. That is what makes the digest an
identifier rather than a timestamp, and it is what the two-process
determinism check on the live service verifies.

THE CAP: more than 20000 runs is refused with the cap named, rather
than silently truncated (a truncated run is a different answer wearing
the same label).

THE LIMITATION IS STATED: the method is IID resampling, which ignores
autocorrelation and the clustering of losing streaks, so the reported
tail UNDERSTATES the risk of a real strategy. A block bootstrap is the
right tool for a serially-correlated series; this service does not
offer one and does not pretend to.

post.summary: Is this market trending or ranging? Signed regime read from your own series (PAID $0.05)
post.description:
Return ONE signed, dated regime read.

Price $0.05 / 50000 atomic per read. The caller submits their own
close series (optionally with high and low); the engine returns
trend_up | trend_down | range | high_vol | low_vol | unknown with a
confidence and the features that produced it.

THE FEATURES ARE REPRODUCIBLE FROM THE SUPPLIED SERIES ONLY. The
slope is a least-squares fit on the bar index; the ATR percentage and
the ADX are computed from the caller's own high/low/close. No external
data source is consulted, no OANDA, no database — so a buyer can
recompute every number from the series they sent.

THE COVERAGE GATE: fewer than 60 bars returns `unknown` with the
count named and a zero confidence. A regime read on 30 bars is a
guess wearing a confidence score.

THREE METHODS: `trend` (the slope's sign and strength), `volatility`
(the last 20 bars against the whole sample) and `combined` (the
volatility regime wins when it is extreme, and the trend decides the
direction otherwise).

post.description:
Return ONE signed, dated batch verdict.

Price $5.00 / 5000000 atomic per batch. The caller submits the items
and the checks to run; the engine returns one row per item, a summary,
and the cross-item overlap.

ORDER IS THE CALLER'S. The results come back in the order the items
were supplied, and the summary counts do not depend on that order.

ONE INSUFFICIENT ITEM DOES NOT FAIL THE BATCH. A thin item is
reported as `insufficient_data` in its OWN row, with the reason, and
every other item is still judged. A batch that dies because one
member is thin is a batch that gets thrown away — which is the whole
reason this route costs $5.00 and not $0.05.

A ROW IS NEVER `deployable` ON ONE LEG. The item's verdict requires
BOTH a significant return stream AND a sizing verdict that is not
ruin-dominant.

AgentForensicsRequest.title: AgentForensicsRequest
AgentForensicsRequest.description:
INTERCONNECT W6 — Product 3 — POST /v1/agent/forensics.

"Reconstruct what actually happened across this payment, and tell me how
well you know it." The caller supplies a WORKFLOW ID, the evidence
records to investigate, and — optionally — the workflow they EXPECTED to
run, so missing and duplicate steps are DETECTED rather than guessed.

`evidence` is a list of signed evidence records (the platform's
`control-plane-event` shape). `expected.steps` is the step list the
workflow was supposed to run. `expected.delivered` and `expected.price`
describe what was delivered and what it was priced at, so a mismatch
between the money paid and the service received is detectable.

Honest-answer boundary: an EMPTY evidence set returns UNRESOLVED, never
a finding. The absence of evidence is not evidence of wrongdoing, and
the engine has no vocabulary for an accusation.

Integrity boundary: the report separates what the records PROVE
(`verified_facts`) from what a third party ASSERTED (`provider_claims`)
from what the engine COMPUTED (`derived_conclusions`) from what it
CANNOT SETTLE (`unresolved`). A valid signature proves the record was
signed by that key; it does not prove the provider delivered anything.

Read-only boundary: the engine reads what it is given and mutates
nothing. It holds no key, contacts no provider and settles nothing.

AgentPreflightRequest.title: AgentPreflightRequest
AgentPreflightRequest.description:
INTERCONNECT W4 — Product 1 — POST /v1/agent/preflight.

"Is this agent workflow ready to execute?" The caller supplies a
WORKFLOW MANIFEST: the steps, the services each step calls, the agent
identity, the planned and maximum spend, the required inputs, and the
evidence/validation rules that apply.

The engine answers with one of FOUR verdicts — READY |
READY_WITH_WARNINGS | BLOCKED | INDETERMINATE — and the checks that
back it.

Honest-answer boundary: READY is NEVER returned because an endpoint is
online. Every REQUIRED requirement in the manifest must have been
VERIFIED, and a requirement whose check could not run caps the verdict
at INDETERMINATE. A capability that cannot be checked is listed in
`checks_not_performed`, which is mandatory and non-empty whenever
anything could not be verified.

Malformed-input boundary: a manifest that is not an object, or that
names no workflow, returns HTTP 422 with a machine-readable error code
and NO stack trace. The engine never guesses a missing step, a missing
requirement or a missing spend figure.

Point-in-time boundary: every check that observed live state carries
`point_in_time: true`, and the response states that a passing
pre-flight does not guarantee future availability, safety or
correctness.

Read-only boundary: the service makes NO outbound call, holds no
budget, reserves nothing, settles nothing and cannot stop a caller
invoking a paid route directly. It is advice, by construction.

AgentReputationRequest.title: AgentReputationRequest
AgentReputationRequest.description:
Service 9 — POST /v1/agent-reputation.
Compute + sign a deterministic reputation composite ('Credit Bureau of the
Agentic Economy') for an agent from its SUPPLIED signed outcome events.
`events`: [{outcome: success|fail|dispute, amount_usd?, ts?, note?}, ...].
The engine (reputation_kb.py) aggregates ONLY the supplied events into a
bounded [0,1] reputation_score + a human-readable verdict. Missing data is
reported honestly as not-provided, never guessed. Deterministic: identical
input -> identical composite + identical SHA-256/Ed25519 signature, so a
caller can regenerate and re-verify the exact bytes free at
GET /v1/agent-reputation/verify.

AttestationReceiptRequest.title: AttestationReceiptRequest
AttestationReceiptRequest.description:
Service 17 — POST /v1/receipts/mint (PAID per-typed-receipt).
Mint a TYPED, signed attestation receipt for any tx/action, wrapped around
the live veritrack-attest spine. A typed receipt schema
{receiptType, tx, action, actor?, subject?, metadata?} distinct from flat
notarization — machine-validable field-by-field, not just byte-replay.

AttestedBriefRequest.title: AttestedBriefRequest
AttestedBriefRequest.description:
Service 5 — POST /v1/research/attested-brief.
Returns a REAL, deterministic, signed+reproducible research brief.

AttestedFinanceRequest.title: AttestedFinanceRequest
AttestedFinanceRequest.description:
Service 8 — POST /v1/finance/attested-evidence.
Assess + attest a financial statement or metrics payload and return SIGNED
reproducible evidence. `statement` may be a dict of figures (aliases like
revenue / revenue_total / net_income / total_assets are tolerated) or a
list of {name|key, value} rows. `company`/`period` are optional provenance
metadata carried verbatim. The engine NEVER downloads/fabricates market
data — every finding derives only from the supplied figures.

AuditEvidencePackageRequest.title: AuditEvidencePackageRequest
AuditEvidencePackageRequest.description:
Service 52 — POST /v1/audit/evidence-package (PAID per package).

The caller submits the artifacts it holds plus the claims it wants to
make about them.

Safe-deny boundary: an artifact with neither content nor content_ref is
EXCLUDED from the Merkle set and named in `gaps` — never hashed from
nothing. An artifact with no provenance is reported with
`provenance: null` and a named gap, and it does NOT contribute to any
assertion's basis.

No-lookahead boundary: the engine is a pure function of the caller's own
artifacts and assertions. It contacts no source, resolves no
reference and reads no clock.

Read-only boundary: this service NEVER settles, debits, or moves funds.
The only on-chain movement is the price of the answer.

`arrival` is REQUIRED in substance: implementation shortfall is

BioAuditReceiptRequest.title: BioAuditReceiptRequest
BioAuditReceiptRequest.description:
BioTrust Service 06 — POST /v1/bio/audit/receipts (PAID per receipt).

Create ONE signed, offline-verifiable record of an administrative
biosecurity check. The `subject` is HASHED, never stored, so a
confidential identifier never lands in a receipt that may be shared.

`check_type` is restricted to the engine's allow-list; anything else
is refused with a structured error, not accepted and not generalised.
`outcome_category` is the CALLER's own label, reproduced verbatim.

BioAuditVerifyRequest.title: BioAuditVerifyRequest
BioAuditVerifyRequest.description:
BioTrust Service 06b — POST /v1/bio/audit/verify (PAID per verification).

Verify a receipt a THIRD PARTY issued. The receipt carries its own
`public_key`, so a caller can verify it offline for free; this paid
sibling is for the case where the caller wants an independent party to
do the check and state the verdict in a signed response.

BioComplianceQueryRequest.title: BioComplianceQueryRequest
BioComplianceQueryRequest.description:
BioTrust Service 02 — POST /v1/bio/compliance/query (PAID per query).

Retrieve CITED passages from the official biosafety-guidance corpus,
report conflicts between sources without resolving them, or diff two
versions of a document.

The corpus is a POINT-IN-TIME SNAPSHOT built at deploy time; this
call NEVER fetches. The answer carries the corpus's `built_at`, so
the caller always knows how current the text is.

`compare` switches the service into version-compare mode and takes
exactly two `doc_id`s. It reports metadata deltas and section-level
differences; it does not interpret them.

BioLabAssetsReconcileRequest.title: BioLabAssetsReconcileRequest
BioLabAssetsReconcileRequest.description:
BioTrust Service 09 — POST /v1/bio/labassets/reconcile (PAID per report).

Reconcile declared custody records and produce an accountability
report.

`item_class` is a CLOSED vocabulary: `biological_sample`, `reagent`,
`equipment`, `document` or `consumable`. Anything else is reported
as `unclassified_item` — a record defect, not a request error.

The schema carries NO free-text field, and unknown top-level keys
are refused rather than ignored. `as_of` is required: a
reconciliation needs the instant it is reconciled at.

BioLabCyberEventsRequest.title: BioLabCyberEventsRequest
BioLabCyberEventsRequest.description:
BioTrust Service 08 — POST /v1/bio/labcyber/events (PAID per pass).

Run eight DOCUMENTED rules over the caller's own security events.

The rule set is fixed and published. A caller may NOT inject a rule:
a caller-supplied rule is a data-exfiltration channel wearing a
policy hat, so there is no rule-injection surface at all.

A request whose events carry a credential-bearing key (matching
`password|passwd|secret|token|api_key|credential`) is REFUSED with a
structured error — this service does not ingest credentials, and the
refusal never echoes the value.

BioOutbreakEventsRequest.title: BioOutbreakEventsRequest
BioOutbreakEventsRequest.description:
BioTrust Service 05 — POST /v1/bio/outbreak/events (PAID per query).

Normalise official public-health notices into deduplicated,
revision-tracked, freshness-flagged events an agent can filter and
cite.

The `since`/`until` filters are ISO-8601 instants; the `geography`
and `category` filters are matched against the curated lexicons;
`source_ids` narrows to a subset of the two wired feeds. `refresh`
forces a refetch past the 600-second cache TTL.

The response's `status` is `degraded` when a source could not be
reached and no fresh cache existed for it — the working sources are
still returned.

BioProvenanceVerifyRequest.title: BioProvenanceVerifyRequest
BioProvenanceVerifyRequest.description:
BioTrust Service 12 — POST /v1/bio/provenance/verify (PAID per verify).

Verify the origin, integrity and version history of an approved
dataset, from the manifest the caller supplies.

NO FILE IS UPLOADED and no dataset content passes through this
service — only hashes and metadata. The `files` list carries a name,
a SHA-256 digest, an optional size, an optional version and an
optional parent digest.

`expected` is the caller's own set of expectations. Each entry may
carry `source`, `licence`, `file_count` and `root_sha256`; only the
keys that are present are checked.

BioResearchReviewRequest.title: BioResearchReviewRequest
BioResearchReviewRequest.description:
BioTrust Service 11 — POST /v1/bio/research-reviews (PAID per record).

One action per call. The `action` selects which fields matter.

The service RECORDS a human dual-use review process. It never
decides: every decision in the record was made by a named human. The
category vocabulary is a checklist of nine labels, not a
risk-assessment methodology, and no decision made here is a safety
determination.

BioRiskAssessRequest.title: BioRiskAssessRequest
BioRiskAssessRequest.description:
BioTrust Service 01 — POST /v1/bio/risk/assess (PAID per assessment).

A STRUCTURED REVIEW RECORD over a declared institutional setup. It is
NOT a biological assessment: the service does not score a pathogen,
does not rank an agent's danger, and does not infer hazard from
anything the caller did not explicitly declare.

THE SCHEMA IS ENUM-ONLY, AND THAT IS A SAFETY CONTROL. There is no
free-text field anywhere in this request. Every field is an enum, a
bounded list of enums, or a bounded identifier. A pathogen name, a
sequence, a method, a quantity and a protocol have nowhere to go: a
request that tries to supply one is REFUSED with `unknown_field`
before it reaches the engine. Do not add a `description` or a
`notes` field — that would open the injection surface and the
dual-use surface at once.

`project_id_hash` is the CALLER's hash of its own project identifier.
This service receives the hash and never the identifier, so the
confidential identifier does not enter a record that may be shared,
logged or filed.

`policy_ref` names a `doc_id` from the compliance corpus. If it does
not resolve, the answer is `insufficient_information` — the
assessment cannot cite a policy that does not resolve, so it cannot
assert a tier on the basis of one.

`as_of` is REQUIRED: an assessment needs the instant it is made at,
and this service does not read the clock.

`model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` is LOAD-BEARING, not
decoration. Pydantic's default is `extra="ignore"`, which SILENTLY
DROPS an unrecognised field — so a request carrying `pathogen` or
`sequence` would be accepted, the field would vanish, and the caller
would believe the service had assessed it. That was MEASURED on this
platform before this line was added: every /v1/bio/* route dropped
unknown fields without a word. `extra="forbid"` turns that silence
into a 422 with a named field, and the engine's own `unknown_field`
guard then produces the structured refusal with the field list.

BioTrustProvidersRequest.title: BioTrustProvidersRequest
BioTrustProvidersRequest.description:
BioTrust Service 13 — POST /v1/bio/trust/providers (PAID per record).

A registry of provider claims that can be checked. A claim may be
labelled `verified` only when its signature verifies AND it carries
a methodology AND it carries an evidence link; otherwise the
registry downgrades it to `self_reported` and records why.

`verified` means "signature-verified claim by a named key holder" and
nothing more. It is not "true", "safe", "audited" or "certified".
There is no score, no rank and no star rating anywhere in this
service's response.

BioVerificationChecksRequest.title: BioVerificationChecksRequest
BioVerificationChecksRequest.description:
BioTrust Service 14 — POST /v1/bio/verification/checks (PAID per check).

ONE check per call. `check` selects the registry, and `query` carries
the identifiers for that registry.

The service VERIFIES THE EXISTENCE and STANDING of a researcher, an
institution, a publication or a company against public registries, and
screens a name against official sanctions lists. It does NOT verify
personal identity documents (KYC) and it does NOT verify professional
credentials — both are out of scope, and the response says so.

`purpose` is REQUIRED and is recorded for accountability: the reason a
check runs travels with the answer, so an unrecorded check is not
accountable.

`min_score` applies to the sanctions check only. It is the Jaccard
threshold for a token-overlap candidate, and it can never be relaxed
to make a screen look cleaner than it is.

BioWorkflowRequest.title: BioWorkflowRequest
BioWorkflowRequest.description:
BioTrust Service 10 — POST /v1/bio/workflows (PAID per decision).

One action per call. The `action` selects which fields matter, and
the engine refuses a call whose fields do not match the action.

The service RECORDS AND ROUTES a human decision process. It does not
perform, validate or score the risk assessment a biosafety review is
about, and an approval recorded here is a record of a human's
decision — not evidence that a facility is safe.

BudgetPreflightRequest.title: BudgetPreflightRequest
BudgetPreflightRequest.description:
Service 23 — POST /v1/budget/preflight (PAID per-decision).
A machine-native agent-safety primitive: a budget/policy preflight gate an
agent calls BEFORE any spend. Caller supplies {agent_id, action_amount_usd,
policy {per_tx_cap, daily_cap, spent_today}}; the engine deterministically
evaluates the proposed action amount against the supplied policy and
returns a signed allow/deny with remaining_budget_usd. Safe-deny boundary:
any malformed input returns decision "deny" (NEVER defaults to allow).
Deterministic pure-function engine (budget_gate_kb.py): no lookahead, no
leaks, no fabricated data; the gate NEVER settles, debits, or moves funds,
and the caller's spent_today is caller-attested (the gate keeps no ledger),
so identical inputs re-checked produce byte-exact the SAME decision.

C2paVerifyRequest.title: C2paVerifyRequest
C2paVerifyRequest.description:
Service 22b — POST /v1/data/c2pa/verify (PAID per-verify).
Given a caller-supplied content hash (64-char lowercase hex, 0x prefix
optional) + C2PA-style manifest claim, deterministically verify the
provenance chain and emit ONE signed attestation covering well-formedness,
content binding (caller-supplied hash <-> manifest-declared asset hash),
extracted creator/generator/software_agent metadata, signature/timestamp/
assertion/ingredient counts, structural integrity (manifest_version,
has_signature, has_timestamp, content_binding_present), and an overall
deterministic verdict (AUTHENTIC / SUSPICIOUS / MALFORMED) with issue
strings. Optional caller-supplied expected_creator / expected_generator
are compared verbatim. Deterministic pure-function engine (c2pa_kb.py):
no lookahead, no leaks, no fabricated data; no live network call is made
during the paid analysis, so the same inputs re-analysed against the same
anchor produce byte-exact the SAME attestation. Signed output is persisted
under attestation_id and read back FREE at
GET /v1/data/c2pa/attestation/{attestation_id}.

ComplianceCheckRequest.title: ComplianceCheckRequest
ComplianceCheckRequest.description:
Client submits a description of an AI use-case or asset scope.

Fields mirror ComplianceForge asset shape so the real Annex III rule set
operates on real, meaningful inputs.

type.title: Type
type.description: One of: artifact_hash | receipt_verified | output_verified | time_elapsed | attestation_present. An unsupported type is INDETERMINATE with the supported vocabulary named.

expected_sha256.title: Expected Sha256
expected_sha256.description: artifact_hash: the expected sha256 hex digest.

observed_sha256.title: Observed Sha256
observed_sha256.description: artifact_hash: the observed sha256 hex digest. If absent and an `artifact` is supplied, the digest is recomputed from it.

artifact.title: Artifact
artifact.description: artifact_hash / output_verified: the payload to hash or verify.

tx_hash.title: Tx Hash
tx_hash.description: receipt_verified: the transaction hash to read.

expected_amount_atomic.title: Expected Amount Atomic
expected_amount_atomic.description: receipt_verified: the required amount in atomic USDC units.

asset.title: Asset
asset.description: receipt_verified: 'USDC' or the USDC address. Anything else is a coverage gap, not a verdict.

payer.title: Payer
payer.description: receipt_verified: the expected payer address. When both payer and payee are supplied, the service's own settlement rule set is run and must say SETTLED.

claims.title: Claims
claims.description: output_verified: the claims to check the artifact against.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: output_verified: what the artifact is about.

after.title: After
after.description: time_elapsed: the ISO-8601 instant the condition becomes true.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: time_elapsed: the ISO-8601 evaluation instant. Supply it for a byte-identical digest across runs.

attestation_id.title: Attestation Id
attestation_id.description: attestation_present: the attestation id to look for.

ConditionalConditionModel.title: ConditionalConditionModel
ConditionalConditionModel.description:
One release condition. `type` selects the evaluator; the rest of the
fields are read by that evaluator only.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.description: The conditions to evaluate. An empty list yields verdict 'hold' — never 'release'.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: The evaluation instant, ISO-8601. Pinned into the evidence core so the digest is reproducible.

body.title: Body
body.description: The canonical evidenceCore from the paid response.

ConditionalVerifyRequest.title: ConditionalVerifyRequest
ConditionalVerifyRequest.description: The signed verdict, to be re-verified.

ContainmentRegisterRequest.title: ContainmentRegisterRequest
ContainmentRegisterRequest.description:
Service 14 — POST /v1/containment/register (PAID per-registration).
Register an agent/custodian's emergency-contact DID, declared policy, and
signed 'if condition X, notify/throttle' rules. Synthex Forge ATTESTES
readiness and RELAYS signal directives only — it NEVER holds kill-switch
execution authority. Deterministic pure-function engine
(containment_kb.py): no lookahead, no leaks, no fabricated data.

ContractTermExtractRequest.title: ContractTermExtractRequest
ContractTermExtractRequest.description:
Service 53 — POST /v1/contract/term-extract (PAID per document).

The caller submits the agreement as text, or as base64 bytes (a PDF or
a text document).

Safe-deny boundary: a document with no locatable clause produces a
signed record with EMPTY clause blocks, a named gap per clause group,
and an ambiguity for every group the engine could not locate. The
engine NEVER invents a party, a date, a price, a cap or a jurisdiction.

No-lookahead boundary: the engine is a pure function of the supplied
text. It reads no clock, no file and no network.

Read-only boundary: this service NEVER settles, debits, or moves funds.
The only on-chain movement is the price of the answer.

CorpusAnchorDocument.title: CorpusAnchorDocument
CorpusAnchorDocument.description: One document in the set being anchored.

CounterpartyObservations.title: CounterpartyObservations
CounterpartyObservations.description:
The CALLER'S OWN observations of the counterparty.

The engine holds no counterparty database, fetches nothing and looks
nothing up. The caller supplies what it has observed; the engine scores
it deterministically.

CounterpartyScoreRequest.title: CounterpartyScoreRequest
CounterpartyScoreRequest.description: Service 1.2 — the counterparty credit & conduct score.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: Who the credential is for, e.g. 'did:agent:abc'.

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.description: The scopes to grant. Every scope must be in the documented vocabulary; an unknown scope is a 400 with the vocabulary in the body. A wildcard is refused.

ttl_seconds.title: Ttl Seconds
ttl_seconds.description: How long the credential is valid, in seconds (1..2592000).

policy_ref.title: Policy Ref
policy_ref.description: The policy the credential is issued under. Its SHA-256 is carried in the credential.

max_uses.title: Max Uses
max_uses.description: How many uses the credential is granted (1..100000).

issued_for.title: Issued For
issued_for.description: Who the credential was issued to, for the record.

credential_token.title: Credential Token
credential_token.description: The compact credential token issued by POST /v1/credentials/issue.

required_scope.title: Required Scope
required_scope.description: Optional: when supplied, the credential must carry this scope or the check fails with credential_scope.

DataValidateRequest.title: DataValidateRequest
DataValidateRequest.description:
Service 54 — POST /v1/data/validate (PAID per validation).

The payload to check, and the schema to check it against.

DataValidateVerifyRequest.title: DataValidateVerifyRequest
DataValidateVerifyRequest.description:
FREE verification body — the canonical evidenceCore plus its digest
and signature, as returned by the paid route.

DecisionAttestRequest.title: DecisionAttestRequest
DecisionAttestRequest.description:
Service 50 — POST /v1/decision/attest (PAID per decision).

The caller submits the decision it is about to take, the evidence it
relies on, and (optionally) its OWN declared policy set.

Safe-deny boundary: a missing actor, decision or policy yields a 200
with the signed record and a DEGRADED assurance — never a fabricated
actor and never an invented rationale. The record names what was
missing in `unknowns`.

No-lookahead boundary: the engine is a pure function of the caller's own
inputs. It reads no clock, no policy registry, no key server and no
network, so there is nothing to look ahead to. `as_of` is a SUPPLIED
input.

DependencyRiskRequest.title: DependencyRiskRequest
DependencyRiskRequest.description:
Service 6 — POST /v1/security/dependency-risk.
Assess + pin the dependency/supply-chain risk of a software dependency
tree and return SIGNED reproducible evidence. `dependencies` entries may
be dicts {"name": ..., "version": ...} or strings "name@version" / "name".

claim.title: Claim
claim.description: {obligation, claimed_by, against}. The obligation is a human sentence; the engine parses the required row count and the required coverage window out of it, and reports what it could not read.

contract.title: Contract
contract.description: {artifact_requirements, required_rows?, required_window?}. The machine-readable requirement WINS over the parsed sentence.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: {buyer: [...], seller: [...]}. Each entry is a {kind, content, manifest, sha256, tx_hash} evidence item.

policy.title: Policy
policy.description: {on_partial: 'pro_rata'}. The split formula is published and fixed; this records the caller's declared policy.

body.title: Body
body.description: The canonical evidenceCore from the paid response.

DisputeVerifyRequest.title: DisputeVerifyRequest
DisputeVerifyRequest.description: The signed ruling, to be re-verified.

date.title: Date
date.description: UTC calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD. Empty = today (UTC).

EconomyAnchorRequest.title: EconomyAnchorRequest
EconomyAnchorRequest.description: Which UTC date to anchor. Defaults to today.

records.title: Records
records.description: The corpus records the anchor was computed over. The root is recomputed from THESE and compared with the published one.

body.title: Body
body.description: The anchor body exactly as it was served (it carries the published corpus_root).

manifest.title: Manifest
manifest.description: The manifest exactly as it was served.

EconomyAnchorVerifyRequest.title: EconomyAnchorVerifyRequest
EconomyAnchorVerifyRequest.description: The records + body + manifest to verify.

query.title: Query
query.description: Free-text capability match against the observed catalogue (path + summary + declared tags). Empty string = all. Supports a substring match and a token AND-match.

max_price_usd.title: Max Price Usd
max_price_usd.description: Price ceiling in USD. An endpoint whose price we have NOT observed is EXCLUDED from a price-filtered query — an unknown price is not a cheap price.

network.title: Network
network.description: CAIP-2 network filter, e.g. 'eip155:8453'. Empty = any.

min_uptime_pct.title: Min Uptime Pct
min_uptime_pct.description: Uptime floor in percent. An endpoint we cannot yet score (fewer than 3 observations) is EXCLUDED — we do not guess.

require_conformance.title: Require Conformance
require_conformance.description: When true, drop every endpoint whose conformance is 'insufficient_observations'.

EconomyIndexRequest.title: EconomyIndexRequest
EconomyIndexRequest.description: The index query. Every field is optional; empty query = everything.

instrument.title: Instrument
instrument.description: The instrument to look up, e.g. 'USD_JPY'. NORMALISED: USDJPY, USD/JPY, usd-jpy and USD_JPY are all one instrument. Aliases: XAUUSD/gold -> XAU_USD, XAGUSD/silver -> XAG_USD, SPX500 -> SPX500_USD, NAS100 -> NAS100_USD.

timeframe.title: Timeframe
timeframe.description: The timeframe to look up, e.g. 'H1'. NORMALISED: 60m == H1, 1h == H1, 4h == H4, 1d == D1.

strategy_type.title: Strategy Type
strategy_type.description: The strategy type, e.g. 'donchian_breakout'. Case and separator insensitive: 'Donchian Breakout' == 'donchian_breakout'.

family.title: Family
family.description: The strategy family, e.g. 'breakout'. Case and separator insensitive.

free_text.title: Free Text
free_text.description: A free-text description, matched on normalised token overlap against the entry's name, type, family and edge_type. Generic words ('strategy', 'backtest', 'using') are stopwords and carry no matching signal.

EdgePriorRequest.title: EdgePriorRequest
EdgePriorRequest.description:
The prior-test query. Every field is optional; at least ONE must be
supplied or the route answers 400 with the accepted field list.

returns.title: Returns
returns.description: The return series, as a JSON list of numbers. EITHER this or 'returns_csv_b64' is required, never both. At most 200000 observations; a longer series is a 400 naming the limit. NaN and infinity are rejected — they are not a return series.

returns_csv_b64.title: Returns Csv B64
returns_csv_b64.description: The return series as a base64-encoded CSV, one number per row. The alternative to 'returns'. Decoded size is capped at 1 MB.

frequency.title: Frequency
frequency.description: 'daily' or 'per_trade'. REQUIRED. A daily series is annualised with sqrt(252); a per_trade series is reported PER TRADE and is never annualised, because a per-trade series has no knowable trades-per-year.

trials_attempted.title: Trials Attempted
trials_attempted.description: How many configurations you tried before keeping this one. REQUIRED, and must be >= 2. This is the number that makes the Deflated Sharpe meaningful: a Sharpe of 2.0 found after 500 tries is priced for what it is. We never assume trials = 1.

claimed.title: Claimed
claimed.description: Optional: {sharpe, cagr, max_dd} — your stated figures. When supplied they are compared against the computed ones and a mismatch is a named finding.

strategy_shape.title: Strategy Shape
strategy_shape.description: Optional: {type, instrument, timeframe}. 'type' is one of trend | mean_reversion | breakout | other and selects the calibration bucket; 'instrument' selects the instrument-class bucket. Instruments are NORMALISED (EUR/USD == EUR_USD == eurusd).

EdgeReplicationRequest.title: EdgeReplicationRequest
EdgeReplicationRequest.description:
The replication request. `returns` (or a base64 CSV), `frequency`
and `trials_attempted` are REQUIRED.

answerCore.title: Answercore
answerCore.description: The answerCore object returned by POST /v1/edge/replication.

output_sha256.title: Output Sha256
output_sha256.description: The output_sha256 returned alongside the answer (optional; when supplied it is compared against a freshly recomputed digest).

answerCore.title: Answercore
answerCore.description: The answerCore object returned by POST /v1/edge/prior.

output_sha256.title: Output Sha256
output_sha256.description: The output_sha256 returned alongside the answer (optional; when supplied it is compared against a freshly recomputed digest).

EnvelopeValidateRequest.title: EnvelopeValidateRequest
EnvelopeValidateRequest.description:
Service 44 — POST /v1/payment/envelope/validate (PAID per-verdict).
A per-counterparty conformance opcode. The caller submits ANY captured x402
402 payment-required envelope (a counterparty's payment proposal) and the
engine returns a signed CONFORMANCE VERDICT over EIGHT named checks:
accepts[] present, payTo recoverable (0x 20-byte EVM), atomic price sane,
CAIP-2 network declared, scheme declared, HTTPS resource, envelope fresh,
x402 version declared.

Safe-deny boundary: a malformed envelope (missing / not an object) is
NON-CONFORMANT with payable=false; the validator NEVER defaults to
conformant. Honesty boundary: a check that CANNOT run is reported
`not_observed` and named in coverage_gaps — never reported as a pass.

Deterministic pure-function engine (envelope_validator_kb.py): no
lookahead, no leaks, no fabricated observations; the validator does NOT
contact the network, does NOT resolve a chain, and NEVER settles, debits,
or moves funds. now_epoch is a SUPPLIED input (not read from the clock)
so the freshness check is byte-exact reproducible.

FinancialPrecisionRequest.title: FinancialPrecisionRequest
FinancialPrecisionRequest.description:
Service 48 — POST /v1/finance/precision (PAID per-calculation).

A per-calculation opcode for finance agents. The caller names ONE
operation and supplies its parameters; the engine computes the figure
in EXACT DECIMAL arithmetic and returns it with the numeric convention
that produced it.

Safe-deny boundary: a missing operation, an unknown operation, a
missing `params` object or a malformed parameter yields HTTP 400 with
verdict "CANNOT_DETERMINE" and NO result — the service never returns a
partial or plausible-looking number on bad input.

Convention boundary: `conventions` may only override `roundingMode`,
`outputScale` and `paymentScale`. Any other key is IGNORED and named
in a finding — it never silently changes a number.

No-lookahead boundary: the engine is a pure function of the caller's
own numbers. It reads no clock, no price feed, no rate feed, no
calendar and no database, so there is nothing to look ahead to.

Read-only boundary: this service NEVER settles, debits, or moves
funds. The only on-chain movement is the price of the calculation.

ForensicsIngestRequest.title: ForensicsIngestRequest
ForensicsIngestRequest.description:
Service 10 — POST /v1/evidence/ingest.
Seal one signed-attribution / forensics evidence record ('who did what' —
actor DID, action, action hash, timestamps) into a tamper-evident vault
entry. The engine (forensics_kb.py) is a PURE FUNCTION of the supplied
evidence; missing fields are reported honestly, action_hash is derived
deterministically when not supplied, never guessed. Deterministic: identical
input -> identical entryId + identical SHA-256/Ed25519 signature, so an
auditor can regenerate and re-verify the exact bytes free at
GET /v1/evidence/verify.

ForensicsQueryRequest.title: ForensicsQueryRequest
ForensicsQueryRequest.description:
Service 10 — POST /v1/evidence/query (PAID per-query).
Bind a set of sealed forensics-vault entries (as returned by /ingest) into
ONE signed, SHA-256-reproducible query receipt, optionally filtered to an
actor. Deterministic: identical entry set -> identical receipt digest +
Ed25519 signature, re-verifiable free at GET /v1/evidence/verify.

IdentityAgentEvidence.title: IdentityAgentEvidence
IdentityAgentEvidence.description: One piece of evidence supporting the binding.

IdentityControlRequest.title: IdentityControlRequest
IdentityControlRequest.description:
Service 18 — POST /v1/identity/control-proof (PAID per signed
control-proof). Non-determinative signed claim that an entity controls an
identifier (key/DID/wallet). Wraps the live veritrack-attest spine into a
TYPED, signed CONTROL-PROOF. Compliant boundary: it attests DOCUMENTED
CONTROL of an identifier — it does NOT determine KYC / real-world identity.

IndexX402Request.title: IndexX402Request
IndexX402Request.description:
Service 2.1 — the dated agentic-commerce index.

NOTE ON `date`: it is a SUPPLIED input, never the wall clock. The index
is a MARK, and a mark is for a date. The same request always produces
byte-identical canonical bytes and therefore a byte-identical
`output_sha256` and signature.

JudgeGradeRequest.title: JudgeGradeRequest
JudgeGradeRequest.description:
Service 16 — POST /v1/mcp/eval/judge (PAID per-pair).
Grade ONE caller-supplied response pair (candidate vs reference/gold) against
a rubric and return a SIGNED, SHA-256-reproducible grade. Honest,
deterministic pure-function engine (judge_kb.py): no lookahead, no leaks,
no fabricated data; a numeric grade is withheld when no rubric criterion is
assessable (INSUFFICIENT-DATA). No external LLM inference — the grade is a
deterministic function of the supplied strings + rubric, which is the
x402-native differentiator: a signed, reproducible, machine-verifiable eval
verdict an automation loop can prove.

dataset.title: Dataset
dataset.description: The dataset the question is about, e.g. 'OANDA v20 candles'.

licence_spdx.title: Licence Spdx
licence_spdx.description: The licence under which the data is held, as an SPDX id (MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0, CC-BY-NC-4.0, proprietary-vendor-tos, ...). OPTIONAL: if omitted, the dataset is matched against the corpus aliases; an unmatched dataset returns verdict 'unknown' with a named coverage gap — never a guess.

intended_use.title: Intended Use
intended_use.description: What you intend to do with the data. One of: analyse, embed, aggregate, display, redistribute, resell, train.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction the use happens in, e.g. 'EU'. Recorded on the signed record; corpus v1 does not vary by jurisdiction.

answerCore.title: Answercore
answerCore.description: The answerCore object returned by POST /v1/licence/check.

output_sha256.title: Output Sha256
output_sha256.description: The output_sha256 returned alongside the answer (optional; when supplied it is compared against a freshly recomputed digest).

MandateComplianceRequest.title: MandateComplianceRequest
MandateComplianceRequest.description: Service 1.3 — the signed mandate compliance certificate.

MandateObservations.title: MandateObservations

batch_manifest.partial_failures and the batch still settles.

MarketHistoryRequest.title: MarketHistoryRequest
MarketHistoryRequest.description:
Service 49 — POST /v1/market/history (PAID $1.00 per bar series).

The RANGE route. `POST /v1/market/snapshot` is the TAIL route (the
latest N bars of one instrument); the two must never return the same
thing, so an explicit [start, end] window belongs here.

The data served is the Binance official public bulk archive and the
European Central Bank euro reference rates. The OANDA FXTrade Rates
are never served — the OANDA API License Agreement forbids it.

series.description: Must be an object. The handler rejects a null or non-object value with 400 `bad_request`.

MarketHistoryVerifyRequest.description: All of `series`, `manifest` must be supplied. The handler rejects a body missing any of them with 400 `bad_request`.

MarketHoursRequest.title: MarketHoursRequest
MarketHoursRequest.description:
Service 49 — POST /v1/market/calendar (PAID per-schedule opcode).

A per-schedule opcode for trading and settlement agents. The caller
names ONE venue and ONE operation; the engine answers from our own
static, cross-validated session and holiday tables and returns the
answer with the timezone, the DST offset in force on the date, and
the settlement convention that produced it.

Safe-deny boundary: a missing venue, an unknown venue, a missing
operation, an unknown operation, a missing or malformed `tradeDate`
and a non-integer `nowEpoch` all yield HTTP 400 with verdict
"CANNOT_DETERMINE" and NO result — the service never returns a
partial or plausible-looking session time on bad input.

No-single-answer boundary: a date OUTSIDE the baked table coverage
window, and a trade date on a day the venue was shut, are reported as
named CANNOT_DETERMINE verdicts with the coverage gap attached —
never a guessed session time or an invented settlement date.

No-lookahead boundary: the engine is a pure function of the caller's
own inputs plus our own static tables. It reads no clock, no live
calendar feed, no price feed and no database, so there is nothing to
look ahead to. The `nowEpoch` anchor is a SUPPLIED input.

Read-only boundary: this service NEVER settles, debits, or moves
funds. The only on-chain movement is the price of the answer.

MarketSnapshotRequest.title: MarketSnapshotRequest
MarketSnapshotRequest.description:
Service 45 — POST /v1/market/snapshot (PAID per-snapshot).

A per-decision opcode for trading and finance agents. The caller names an
instrument, a granularity and (optionally) an as-of window; the engine
reads the REAL OHLCV rows out of OUR OWN PostgreSQL oanda_ohlcv store and
returns them sealed in a signed, hash-chained, replayable record.

Safe-deny boundary: a malformed instrument, an unknown granularity, an
unparseable timestamp or a reversed window returns HTTP 400 with verdict
"CANNOT_DETERMINE" — the service NEVER defaults to a successful snapshot
on bad input. An instrument that is not in the store, or a window with no
rows, returns verdict "CANNOT_DETERMINE" with a named reason; it is
NEVER presented as an empty-but-successful snapshot.

Bounded-scan boundary: `limit` is clamped to [1, 20000] server-side and
every read is an indexed range scan on the (instrument, granularity, time)
primary key. An unbounded request can never reach the 123M-row table.

Historical-data boundary: this is HISTORICAL DATA, not a live price
oracle. The `asOf` field reports the timestamp of the NEWEST BAR IN THE
SNAPSHOT, not the wall clock. It carries NO settlement meaning and must
not be used to mark a position to market.

MemoryGetRequest.title: MemoryGetRequest
MemoryGetRequest.description:
Service 11 — POST /v1/memory/get (PAID per-get).
Return the latest signed, SHA-256-reproducible sealed state record for a
memory key of an agent, so a later session can verify continuity. Honest:
a missing key returns NOT-FOUND (never guessed).

MemoryPutRequest.title: MemoryPutRequest
MemoryPutRequest.description:
Service 11 — POST /v1/memory/put (PAID per-put).
Persist ONE budget-capped state version for an agent's memory key, append it
to that agent's hash-chained continuity store, and return an Ed25519-signed
+ SHA-256-reproducible sealed record with a reproducible `stateHash` that
commits to the previous chain head. Budget-capped (up to) via
max_value_bytes. Deterministic: identical (owner,key,value) after the same
chain head -> identical stateHash + signature.

NavAttestRequest.title: NavAttestRequest
NavAttestRequest.description:

PortfolioRiskRequest.title: PortfolioRiskRequest
PortfolioRiskRequest.description:
Service 51 — POST /v1/portfolio/risk (PAID per report).

The caller submits its positions and the risk model it intends to use.

Safe-deny boundary: a malformed notional or an unresolvable side is
EXCLUDED from the report and named in `warnings` — never treated as
zero and never assumed long.

No-lookahead boundary: the engine is a pure function of the caller's own
numbers. It fetches NO market data, looks up NO volatility and infers NO
correlation. A missing vol is reported as `vol_assumed: none-supplied`
and the risk grade is degraded accordingly.

Read-only boundary: this service NEVER settles, debits, or moves funds.
The only on-chain movement is the price of the answer.

QuotaPreflightRequest.title: QuotaPreflightRequest
QuotaPreflightRequest.description:
Service 47 — POST /v1/quota/preflight (PAID per-reservation).

A per-outbound-call guardrail for ANY agent that calls third parties. An
agent that is about to make an outbound call asks this gate FIRST: "may I
make this call, given the quota I am attesting to?" The engine reserves
the call against a DURABLE, ATOMIC quota ledger and returns a signed
ALLOW / DENY that proves what the agent was told and what it consumed.

Safe-deny boundary: a missing agent id, a missing target, a zero or
non-integer call count, or a missing/invalid quota returns HTTP 400 with
decision "deny" — the service NEVER defaults to allow on bad input.

Store-outage boundary: if the reservation ledger cannot be read, the
verdict is CANNOT_DETERMINE, NEVER allow. A quota gate that allowed
during a ledger outage would be precisely the runaway it exists to stop.

Stale-window boundary: if the agent attests a quota window that has
already rolled over, the verdict is DENY with a "stale-window" reason —
never a silent reset of the agent's consumption.

The caller's `usedCalls` is CALLER-ATTESTED input. The service compares it
against its own stored consumption and names any disagreement; the STORED
count is the authority for the reservation.

Read-only boundary: this service does NOT make the outbound call, and
never settles, debits, holds, or moves funds. The only on-chain movement
is the price of the decision itself.

ReadinessAttestRequest.title: ReadinessAttestRequest
ReadinessAttestRequest.description:
Service 19 — POST /v1/readiness/attest (PAID per signed
containment-readiness attestation). Signature wrap of the live
veritrack-attest spine: attests, from caller-supplied readiness evidence,
that a system/component/service is containment-ready per a supplied policy
snapshot. Deterministic pure-function engine (readiness_kb.py): carries
caller fields verbatim, rejects missing required fields, no lookahead/leaks/
fabrication, NO kill-switch execution authority (boundary). Verify free.

RedteamAuthScanRequest.title: RedteamAuthScanRequest
RedteamAuthScanRequest.description:
Service 22 — POST /v1/security/redteam/authorized-scan (PAID per-assessment).
Authorized/adversarial-testing-as-a-service behind a PROVABLE authorization
gate: {target_url, authorized_tests[], authorization_evidence[],
scope_description?} -> {gate_outcome, compliance_grade, planned_tests[],
attestation_id, sha256, ed25519Sig}. The engine REFUSES to run unless the
caller supplies at least ONE well-formed authorization proof (DNS/TXT or
.well-known token hash, or signed scoped permit). Every refusal is itself
signed + anchored so the service can PROVE it only ever ran on
authorization. Deterministic pure-function engine (redteam_kb.py): no
lookahead, no leaks, no fabricated data; NO live probe / DNS lookup / HTTP
fetch is made during the paid assessment — the gate is validated by hash
equality against the caller-supplied expected-token hash. Signed output is
keyed by attestation_id and re-checkable FREE at
POST /v1/security/redteam/recheck.

RouteExecuteDestination.description: Where the money is meant to land.

RouteExecuteIntent.title: RouteExecuteIntent
RouteExecuteIntent.description: What the caller wants to move.
