RouteExecuteRequest.description: The intent and the constraints the plan must meet.

SettlementReceiptRequest.title: SettlementReceiptRequest
SettlementReceiptRequest.description:
Service 46 — POST /v1/settlement/receipt (PAID per-verdict).

A per-payment reconciliation opcode for ANY paying agent. The caller
supplies a transaction hash plus the amount, payer and payee it expects;
the engine reads PUBLIC CHAIN STATE and returns a signed
SETTLED / NOT_SETTLED / CANNOT_DETERMINE verdict with the matched USDC
Transfer log, the block number and the confirmation depth it read.

Safe-deny boundary: a malformed tx hash, a non-numeric amount, an
unparseable address or a negative confirmation depth returns HTTP 400
with verdict "CANNOT_DETERMINE" — the service NEVER defaults to
SETTLED or NOT_SETTLED on bad input.

Chain-outage boundary: if the chain cannot be read, the verdict is
CANNOT_DETERMINE, NEVER NOT_SETTLED. A false NOT_SETTLED would make an
agent re-pay an invoice that already settled, so the two are kept
strictly distinct.

Counterparty-receipt boundary: the counterparty's own receipt is
optional. When supplied it is compared field-by-field against the chain
observation and any disagreement is reported as a named finding. It
NEVER overrides the chain-derived verdict — the chain is the oracle.

Read-only boundary: this service NEVER settles, debits, or moves funds.
The only on-chain movement is the price of the verdict itself.

SettlementRouteDestination.title: SettlementRouteDestination
SettlementRouteDestination.description: One place the settlement could land.

SignedSnapshotRequest.title: SignedSnapshotRequest
SignedSnapshotRequest.description:
Service 13 — POST /v1/data/signed-snapshot (PAID per-snapshot).
Seal a caller-supplied data feed (series rows + source citations) into ONE
signed, SHA-256-reproducible provenance envelope with honestly-labelled
freshness evidence. Deterministic pure-function engine (freshness_kb.py):
no lookahead, no leaks, no fabricated data; missing freshness anchors are
reported honestly as NOT-PROVIDED.

price_eur.description: The asking price in EUR. REQUIRED.

ebitda_eur.title: Ebitda Eur
ebitda_eur.description: Annual EBITDA in EUR. REQUIRED. Undisclosed is NOT zero — an undisclosed figure returns insufficient_data, never a model.

sector.description: The sector, free text, e.g. 'Business services — accounting & tax advisory'. Used for Rule B (food service) and for the benchmark bucket. Matching is word-boundary and accent-insensitive.

seller_financing_pct.description: Seller financing offered, as a percentage of price. The house approach is 20-30%, so 20 or more is reported as 'preferred' and less as 'absent'.

SynthesisVerdictRequest.title: SynthesisVerdictRequest
SynthesisVerdictRequest.description:
Service 12 — POST /v1/synthesis/verdict (PAID per-verdict).
Fold three caller-supplied evidence blocks (research / quant / audit) into
ONE signed, SHA-256-reproducible cross-domain synthesis verdict. Honest,
deterministic pure-function engine (synthesis_kb.py): no lookahead, no
leaks, no fabricated data; missing blocks are reported honestly.

TaskAcceptanceSpec.title: TaskAcceptanceSpec
TaskAcceptanceSpec.description: The spec the work is judged against.

ThreatModelAnalyzeRequest.title: ThreatModelAnalyzeRequest
ThreatModelAnalyzeRequest.description:
Service 21a — POST /v1/security/threatmodel (PAID per-analysis).
Given a caller-supplied MCP/A2A tool manifest, produce a signed threat-model
document covering catalogued scopes+permissions, high-risk permission flags
(payment/exec/net/storage/identity), escalation paths, MCP/A2A-specific
attack vectors, a deterministic overall risk grade (low/medium/high/critical),
and concrete recommendations. Caller supplies the manifest verbatim; the
deterministic pure-function engine (threatmodel_kb.py) never invents
permissions or makes a live probe, so the same manifest re-analysed against
the same anchor produces byte-exact the SAME threat model. Signed output is
stored under attestation_id and read back FREE at
GET /v1/security/threatmodel/verify/{attestation_id}.

ToolPermissionThreatModelRequest.title: ToolPermissionThreatModelRequest
ToolPermissionThreatModelRequest.description:
Service 21 — POST /v1/mcp/threatmodel/tool-permission (PAID per-analysis).
Threat-model the caller's OWN MCP/A2A manifest for permission-sprawl
takeover risk: {manifest, ownershipProof?} -> {verdict, overallRiskScore,
riskClassHistogram, sprawlFindings[], sha256, ed25519Sig}. Caller supplies
the manifest (MCP tools/list or normalized A2A skills) + (recommended) an
ownership proof; the engine deterministically scores sprawl into ONE signed,
reproducible risk envelope. CRITICAL (takeover-grade) verdicts are
auth-gated: they require an ownership proof so a takeover risk is only
attested on an attributed manifest. Deterministic pure-function engine
(tool_permission_threatmodel_kb.py): no lookahead, no leaks, no fabricated
data; no live lookup is performed during the paid analysis so the result is
reproducible byte-exact at FREE recheck; nothing is inflated (MINIMAL when
no permission is declared anywhere).

TreasuryAuthorizeRequest.title: TreasuryAuthorizeRequest
TreasuryAuthorizeRequest.description:
INTERCONNECT W5 — Product 2 — POST /v1/agent/treasury/authorize.

Evaluate the policy, then ATOMICALLY reserve the budget.

The policy is evaluated FIRST, so a request the policy refuses never
touches the budget and never writes a reservation row.

`idempotency_key` is scoped to (operation, principal): the same key
under a DIFFERENT principal is a different request, and the same key
under the SAME principal replays the recorded outcome instead of
reserving a second time.

The response states the TRUST BOUNDARY: if the caller can pay a
provider without going through this authorize step, this service
controls nothing.

TreasuryBudgetRequest.title: TreasuryBudgetRequest
TreasuryBudgetRequest.description:
INTERCONNECT W5 — Product 2 — POST /v1/agent/treasury/budget.

Set the budget limit for a scope. The scope is `{"kind": "agent"|
"customer", "id": "..."}`.

The limit is a DECIMAL STRING or a whole number of dollars. A float
is refused by the engine: a float cannot represent a currency amount
exactly, and a budget that is off by a fraction of a cent is not the
budget the caller asked for.

A limit BELOW the money already committed or reserved against the
scope is REFUSED, not applied — a budget that is already breached is
a finding, not a configuration.

TreasuryCommitRequest.title: TreasuryCommitRequest
TreasuryCommitRequest.description:
INTERCONNECT W5 — Product 2 — POST /v1/agent/treasury/commit.

Settle a reservation by proving the payment on the PAYMENT RAIL.

There is deliberately NO success flag in this model. The caller
cannot assert that a payment happened — the settlement is verified
against the rail (the settlement ledger and the on-chain receipt
oracle), and a caller-supplied flag would be exactly the thing the
product exists to prevent.

A transaction whose outcome is AMBIGUOUS is REFUSED here. It must be
reconciled first. A timeout is not a failure, and a duplicate retry
is the failure mode this product prevents.

TreasuryReleaseRequest.title: TreasuryReleaseRequest
TreasuryReleaseRequest.description:
INTERCONNECT W5 — Product 2 — POST /v1/agent/treasury/release.

Release a RESERVED reservation, returning its whole amount — or
RECONCILE an AMBIGUOUS transaction against the payment rail.

`action` is "release" (default) or "reconcile". A reconcile reads
the rail and resolves to SETTLED, RELEASED, or stays AMBIGUOUS. It
NEVER guesses: an unreadable rail resolves to nothing, and no retry
is authorised.

TrustedRouteRequest.title: TrustedRouteRequest
TrustedRouteRequest.description:
Service 9b — POST /v1/agent-reputation/trusted-route (premium routing).
Input: `routes` = list of {route|id|agent, events:[{outcome,...}]}.
Output: a deterministic, Ed25519-signed + SHA-256-reproducible trusted-route
ranking (best first) derived ONLY from the supplied per-route outcome
histories. Routing is decision-support over supplied data — no lookahead,
no external fetches, no fabricated metrics.

UptimeCanaryProbeRequest.title: UptimeCanaryProbeRequest
UptimeCanaryProbeRequest.description:
Service 20 — POST /v1/mcp/verify/uptime (PAID per-probe).
Score ONE uptime-canary probe for an x402 service: {serviceUrl, checks[],
lastConfirmedSettlementTx?} -> {up, lastConfirmedSettlementTx,
settlementLatencyP95, checks[], sha256, ed25519Sig}. Caller supplies the
probe checks + (recommended) the settlement anchor; engine deterministically
scores + signs them. Settlement-anchor presence is the differentiator vs
commodity ping-canaries. Deterministic pure-function engine
(uptime_canary_kb.py): no lookahead, no leaks, no fabricated data; no live
network call is made during the paid probe so the result is reproducible
byte-exact; nothing is inflated (UP-NO-SETTLE when no anchor supplied).

VerdictBatchRequest.title: VerdictBatchRequest
VerdictBatchRequest.description: The items to judge, and the checks to run on them.

VerifyCatalogRegisterRequest.title: VerifyCatalogRegisterRequest
VerifyCatalogRegisterRequest.description:
Service 15 — POST /v1/verify-catalog/register (PAID per-registration).
Register any x402 service's signed output into the PUBLIC network-effect
VERIFY catalog. The catalog re-checks the supplied output (recomputes its
canonical SHA-256), honestly assesses whether a well-formed signature was
supplied, counts network-effect edges (references TO this service from
other catalog entries — the compounding-defensibility mechanism), and grows
an honest trust index 0..1. Deterministic pure-function engine
(verify_catalog_kb.py): no lookahead, no leaks, no fabricated data.
